_method_note: Structured cross-references between locations, time periods, characters, and concepts found across the material set. Every entry lists its source file(s). Nothing here is asserted beyond what a source states; where sources disagree, both values are kept and a matching entry is added to 'conflicts'. Full prose per source lives in context.md; this file is the associative index. Sources are abbreviated: atlax_i, atlax_ii, catastro, ensayo_i, libro, timelines_py (timelines.py), esquema (ESQUEMA.pdf), book_of_inventions, cartography_highways/cartography_trains/cartography_airports (Cartography (Map Markers) [Code].xlsx), luminacion_register (Luminacion Register [Code].xlsx), mapa_del_milenio (El Antiguo Continente de Milkan - Mapa del Milenio.png), plus 5 dated/named screenshots (Khan Ice WP, Sid Nalta WP, Milka General Map, Milka Oceans Plan and Continent Outline, Ruta Lundria-Salthos Cruzados) referenced inline by filename. Per the user (2026-07-24), 'Luminacion Register' and 'Terraforming Regions Purge Register.xlsx' ARE lore sources, split into a narrative layer (named characters/locations/actions - captured under characters.named_inhabitants) and a technical/'mysterious formula' layer (Clock-worldTime triggers, Taterzen movement logic, region-purge flags - left undeciphered, see unknown.md) - not excluded, just not yet interpreted. Some conflict entries also carry a 'user_resolution' field: a design decision the user gave directly (not derived from any document), dated. These sit alongside the documentary facts rather than replacing them. IMPORTANT (2026-07-24): everything above this line, and everything in 'locations'/'time_systems'/'routes'/'characters'/'concepts'/'conflicts' below, is the OBJECTIVE record - reconstructed from primary materials, per the archaeologist method. There is now a second, SUBJECTIVE record: the top-level 'hearsay' array near the end of this file, mirroring _lore/analysis/hearsay.md, logging what characters have actually said in played Blabber dialogues. Hearsay entries are never merged into the objective arrays above and never treated as corroborating them, even when they happen to agree - they are a distinct kind of source, logged separately on purpose.

concepts.notes: not named in any other source; does not obviously correspond to any era boundary in ensayo_i (which places 'Era de la Magia' starting Nov 2025, close to but not matching Ox) or in libro/esquema. See CONFLICT-12

concepts.description: explicit sequence of 'subsistence' starting settlements named in ensayo_i: 1st Puerto Pastizal (era 1), 2nd Okâsia (era 3), 3rd unnamed but enabled by the Vías de Hielo (era 6, 'permitiendo la fundacion de el tercer emplazamiento de subsistencia'), and 5th Nueva Góndola (era 8, explicitly labeled 'quinta aldea de subsistencia').
concepts.notes: the 4th subsistence settlement is never named or described in any source. esquema's year-by-year list names a 'Tercera Aldea Survival' at 2021/576-648 d.V., which lines up date-wise with ensayo_i's unnamed 3rd settlement (era 6, ~582 d.V.) - a plausible name for it, not confirmed since 'Tercera Aldea Survival' reads as a descriptive label rather than a proper name

concepts.description: an institution at Sït:Nâlta; Döran, Forlän, and Forlîas are all described as members/students.
a recurring games/tournament event; first held ~84 d.V. (era 2), where the Görff/Khân-Ice enmity begins; reestablished in Khân-Ice during era 6, in honor of Forlän and Forlîas.

names: hechizo que fuerza a vivir en subsistencia

concepts.notes: not otherwise explained; relationship to Muro Norte / Wasteland (era 7) not stated explicitly, though geographically adjacent (both 'north frontier')

concepts.description: a scoreboard objective demonstrated in Book of Inventions: detects players within 200 blocks of a point over time and displays a 'TOWN' title when the score reaches 1. A working command-mechanic example, not a lore concept.
concepts.notes: presented as a technique/reference snippet, not tied to any specific in-world location or story

conflicts.detail: ensayo_i gives a fully narrated 10-part era system dated in a.V./d.V. against real-world dates 2011-2026. libro gives a separate, only-outlined 6-part 'Venidas'/era system with different names, different boundary years, and no a.V./d.V. framing at all (e.g. libro's 'Era del Daax o de las Maquinas' spans 2018-2020, while ensayo_i's 'Era del Daax' spans only 2018-2019 and 'Era del Confinamiento' covers 2020-2021 separately). Both are kept as distinct systems, not merged.
conflicts.user_resolution: Both timelines coexist in-world as separate, non-overriding reckonings - neither supersedes the other (per user, 2026-07-24).

conflicts.topic: coordinate mismatches for the same named place across sources
conflicts.detail: Khan Ice, Khol Moshin, Sit:Nalta, and Sälthos Cruzados each have coordinate or grid values from two+ sources that do not consistently agree (see each location's 'coords' array and 'notes' field for specifics). Catraniz is the notable exception, where three sources agree exactly.

See concept 'world_name_variants'. Milkantis, Milkäan, Milkantida, and 'Mundo de Milka' are never explicitly related to one another in any source, and libro poses its own unanswered question about whether 'Milkhantida' has another name.
conflicts.user_resolution: Milkantis, Milkantida, and 'Mundo de Milka' are the same world-name with spelling drift over time (per user, 2026-07-24). NOT yet extended to Milkäan: across ensayo_i, catastro, and libro, 'Milkäan' is consistently used as one of two named regions (paired against Platinhëa/Plathinëa), not as a name for the whole world - e.g. catastro's every row is tagged Zona=Milkäan or Zona=Platinhëa, and ensayo_i places 'Puerto Pastizal, en la region de Milkäan' opposite the later-discovered 'region de Plathinëa'. Folding Milkäan into the same-name-as-the-world reading would contradict that regional split, so this is held open pending a direct check with the user rather than applied automatically.

conflicts.detail: Atlax I's dedication names 'PITAGLORIAS' as the inventor/explorer honored by that book. Atlax II's body text refers to the same original-atlas author as 'Fitaglorias'. Treated as the same person under entry 'pitaglorias', but the spelling is not reconciled by any source.

ENSAYO I is credited to 'Iläria desde Lündria', written in an in-world voice. Libro's player roster (Milkucha, Nikkostratos, Termixdelosandes, etc.) does not include this name. Whether 'Iläria' is an in-world persona used by one of the real players, or a distinct authorial identity, is not stated.
conflicts.user_resolution: The credited in-world authors (Pitaglorias/Fitaglorias, Daaxagoras, Storfilias, Iläria) are a mix: some are in-world personas of real players, others are purely legendary/fictional figures with no player behind them (per user, 2026-07-24). Which specific name falls into which category was not yet specified - follow-up needed before this can be applied per-character in the characters.in_world_or_legendary list.

conflicts.topic: founding-year mismatches between catastro and ensayo_i/libro
conflicts.detail: Isla de la Amistad: catastro says 2011, libro's 'Ciudades A.V.' list says 2012. Nalhuë/Ministerio del Tiempo: ensayo_i implies construction started 2023 (798 d.V. era), catastro says 'Inicio' 2024.

atlax_i and image7 both use 'Sid Nalta' (no colon, different second syllable) while ensayo_i, catastro, and libro's prose use 'Sit:Nalta' or 'Sït:Nâlta'. Treated as the same place given the near-identical spelling and shared thematic role (ancient magical fortress/island), but no source confirms this equivalence outright, and the coordinate conflict in CONFLICT-02 does not help resolve it.

'naranja' is Spanish for 'orange', raising the possibility that ensayo_i's 'Villa Naranja' (founded 714 d.V., far east) and catastro's 'Orange Manor' (Platinhëa, start 2024) are the same place under a bilingual name-swap. Dates and described locations do not obviously line up, so this is flagged as unconfirmed, not merged.

ensayo_i/catastro's 'Puerto Tortuga' (a port, Milkäan) and image7's 'Isla Tortuga' (an island, grid 7,3) share the 'Tortuga' name but are described with different generic types (puerto vs isla) and no source states they are the same place.

conflicts.topic: Casa De Esteban vs the legend of Esteban
conflicts.detail: catastro lists a research site called 'Casa De Esteban' (Milkäan). ensayo_i separately references a legendary figure, Esteban, tied to 'el Reloj de Sol', whose legend inspired era 2's maritime exploration. No source explicitly ties the site to the legendary figure.

conflicts.topic: Bahia Pelicanos vs Bahía de las Estatuas
conflicts.detail: catastro lists 'Bahia Pelicanos' (Platinhëa, Hospitality type). ensayo_i and libro separately reference 'Bahía de las Estatuas' as the world's third spawn point and as a listed 'Monumento'. Different names (Pelícanos vs Estatuas); kept as separate entries.

conflicts.topic: a third 'start of the world' reference point, and an unexplained new era-threshold
conflicts.detail: timelines.py's Parallelized Timeline sets its origin O at 2012-07-01, distinct from ensayo_i's stated epoch (0 = 1 enero 2013) and from libro/book_of_inventions's own reference point ('94 SBW, 2022 AD' as the date those books were begun, not the world's origin). The script also introduces 'the Seasons' and 'Eras After the Seasons' (EAS) as a before/after threshold at Ox=2025-12-31, with in-world days running 3x slower afterward - this threshold, and the 3x day-length change, appear nowhere else in the material. Not reconciled with any other source's era boundaries.

conflicts.topic: Aerörea vs Milkäan as Platinhëa's paired continent
conflicts.detail: esquema's poster names Milkäntis's 'dos continentes más importantes' as Aerörea and Platinhëa. Every other source that pairs a region against Platinhëa/Plathinëa (catastro's Zona column, ensayo_i's 'región de Milkäan' vs 'región de Plathinëa', libro's CONTINENTES list) uses 'Milkäan' in that role instead - 'Aerörea' does not appear in any other source at all. This conflict was found after the user's 2026-07-24 resolution of CONFLICT-03 (which covered Milkantis/Milkantida/'Mundo de Milka' but explicitly did not extend to Milkäan) - whether Aerörea is a synonym for Milkäan, a different region entirely, or an error/renaming, is unaddressed.

conflicts.topic: esquema's era-poster names/ranges do not line up 1:1 with ensayo_i's
conflicts.detail: See time_systems.esquema_poster_eras for the full era-by-era comparison. Two patterns recur: (a) same era name, different date range than ensayo_i's era of the same name (e.g. 'Era de los Continentes' = 504-648 d.V. on the poster vs. 664-808 d.V. in ensayo_i); (b) same date range as an ensayo_i era, but a different name (e.g. the poster's 504-648 d.V. range matches ensayo_i's 'Era del Confinamiento' by dates, not by name). This is a third timeline system, found after the user's 2026-07-24 'both timelines coexist' resolution, which was given only for ensayo_i vs. libro's Venidas system - whether that resolution extends to this poster as well is unaddressed.

hearsay._method_note: SUBJECTIVE record, distinct from every array above. Mirrors _lore/analysis/hearsay.md exactly - one entry per real (non-template) dialog file in data/luminacion/blabber/dialogues/. 'claims' are what a character asserted, not verified facts; 'about' cross-references an id in 'locations'/'concepts'/'conflicts' above ONLY to mark topical overlap, never as corroboration. A claim's 'consistent_with_context' field records whether it happens to agree with the objective record as it currently stands - 'true' here is not a guarantee the claim is correct, only that no contradiction has been found yet. Since scripts/sample_lore_knowledge.py draws individual claims from this array into a character's knowledge pool at the same odds as any objective-record fact (see README §8 Step 1), a claim can now be retold by a new character and logged again as a fresh claim. Whenever that happens, scripts/lineage_coin.py rolls a flat 50/50 to decide whether the origin survives the retelling: 'traceable' sets 'derived_from' (a claim id, e.g. 'nawom_morkulo_first_meeting#5') and the dialog line may cite the source by name; 'untraceable' leaves 'derived_from' unset and sets 'oral_lore': true instead - no origin recorded, dialog line uses vague framing ('they say...'), regardless of whether the content itself has drifted. 'oral_lore' can also be set true (paired with a 'note' explaining what grew) on a claim that traces back fine but has still accumulated specifics beyond what its 'about' grounding supports. Most claims have neither field - they're unremarkable, either freshly sampled from the objective record or a faithful, traceable retelling.

entries.summary: A lost traveler arriving in Balhâm meets Sonoros at the rail depot; he orients them, is briefly suspected of being a robber, and explains his work before they part.

claims.text: Balhâm is a 'ciudad sagrada' (sacred city), still mostly unfinished.
Balhâm has been 'going up since 354' - Sonoros explicitly does not know what that number counts from.
claims.note: the not-knowing is itself an accurate reflection of the objective record, which never explains the a.V./d.V. system to a bystander either

claims.text: A monument called 'El Dragón de Balham' exists and is worth seeing.
Rail lines run from Balhâm west to Sälthos Cruzados (~4000 blocks) and east to Khan Ice.
claims.note: matches the 'Khan Ice - Balhâm' and 'Balhâm - Salthos Cruzados' train segments in routes.trains, though Sonoros never cites exact figures - he rounds

claims.text: Sälthos Cruzados is rumored to be the biggest town on the continent - Sonoros does not confirm this, only reports the rumor.
claims.note: the objective record never states which city is 'biggest' at any given moment consistently across eras - see ensayo_i's shifting 'largest city' claims for Sälthos Cruzados, Khân-Ice, and Dragon City at different eras - so this claim is neither confirmed nor contradicted, appropriately left as a rumor

claims.text: Sonoros identifies as being 'out of Görff way' and works walking rail crossings, naming Cruce de Trobal near Khol Moshin as one he checks regularly.
claims.note: Sonoros's profession and Görff connection are invented character texture, not drawn from any material source - see README §8 step 2

entries.summary: Nawom, searching for the road to Puerto Tortuga, meets Morkulo at Nvhi's fountain. Neither knows the way; they trade fragments about each other's home regions and agree to look for a map inside.

claims.text: Neither Nawom nor Morkulo knows the route to Puerto Tortuga.
claims.note: puerto_tortuga is not in either character's sampled knowledge - this is accurate ignorance, not an oversight

claims.text: Nawom is from Terfila, but declines to explain how his family came to be there.
claims.note: Nawom's family origin is a user-given personal fact, not drawn from any material source and not resolved even in Nawom's own knowledge - deliberately left open

claims.text: Morkulo knows of Terfila only via travelers: a banker, Aureobalo, who rides to Khol Moshin, and pilots arriving from Sid Nalta.
claims.note: correctly reflects that 'terfyla' itself was NOT in Morkulo's sampled knowledge, only the named travelers Aureobalo/Nerkeli/Terrolis were

claims.text: Morkulo studied in Tyrnea, 'long enough ago' that he says he barely recognizes who he was then.
claims.note: personal biography, not a material-sourced fact; notably Morkulo's sample also did not include the 'tyrnea' location entry itself, so his firsthand memory is deliberately not backed by (or contradicted by) the objective civic history of the place

claims.text: Nvhi is 'the place they say Därnis heard whatever it was that sent him off to find that new continent.'
claims.note: matches ensayo_i era 9 and the nvhi location entry exactly; Morkulo's own hedge ('they say') is his, not an uncertainty in the source material

claims.text: Morkulo complains that recorded coordinates for Khol Moshin and Khan Ice 'argue with themselves.'
claims.note: an informal, personal echo of CONFLICT-02 - Morkulo is speaking from professional frustration with his own measurements, not citing the analysis

entries.summary: A traveler looking for passage meets Gondarfolas, a sailor at his boat in Görff, and trades a secondhand story - a man who sailed south and never returned, with a search expedition now being organized - for the ride. Gondarfolas recognizes the story as Därnis's, walks through what he's read of it, and traces where his own history books came from.

claims.text: Gondarfolas is based in Görff, sails a small ship ferrying travelers along the coast, and is an avid reader of history.
claims.note: Gondarfolas's trade and reading habit are invented character texture, not drawn from any material source - see README §8 step 2

claims.text: Därnis sailed south out of Sindäara and discovered a new ocean, a burning/volcanic island, and floating land, taken by historians as a sign of a new continent.
Därnis 'came back long enough to tell of it,' before whatever happened to him afterward goes unrecorded.
claims.note: the source (ensayo_i era 9) states what Därnis discovered but does not explicitly confirm he returned to report it - Gondarfolas's reading is a plausible but unconfirmed inference

claims.text: The traveler reports hearing in Khol Moshin that Därnis's siblings are organizing an expedition to search for him, departing from where a highway ends at the continent's southern tip.
claims.note: siblings and a southern-terminus highway appear nowhere in the objective record - genuinely new hearsay, neither corroborated nor contradicted; Gondarfolas explicitly does not confirm it

claims.text: Khol Moshin has no coastline - Gondarfolas, a sailor, has never had reason to go there.
claims.note: khol_moshin's exact geography isn't detailed enough in the objective record to confirm or contradict this outright, though it's consistently treated elsewhere as an inland/rail hub rather than a port

claims.text: Gondarfolas owns two chronicles, the Ensayo and the Libro, and describes them accurately as two histories of the same span of years that never reconcile with each other.
Gondarfolas bought his copies years ago from a trader in Görff he recalls as 'Bracco, or Braggo,' who sold them off cheaply and without explanation.
claims.note: Bracco is invented personal texture, not a material-sourced figure - see README §8 step 2

claims.text: Gondarfolas has no idea where Bracco came from or went afterward.

location.as_named_in_dialog: the Feria del Milenio, by the airplane hangar

entries.summary: Overheard mid-conversation by the player (no player lines - pure eavesdropping), childhood friends Nuvilo and Nerkeli catch up by the hangar Nerkeli is minding for the fair's airplane showcase. They cover codigos and the Daax symbol, Nerkeli's running joke that ducks descend from the Daax, and the highways M9/M7, both of which happen to end at Nvhi - the place Nuvilo's family claims to have founded.

claims.text: Codigos ties to Era del Daax, begun under Gorff's new government, and the Daax symbol was carved into old ruins right around those same years.
claims.note: matches both the codigos and daax_symbol entries; symbol carved c. 372+ d.V. falls within Era del Daax's 360-504 d.V. span

claims.text: Nerkeli jokingly theorizes that ducks are the last living descendants of the Daax.
claims.note: offered explicitly as Nerkeli's own unfounded pet theory, not asserted as history - invented character texture, see README §8 step 2

claims.text: Nuvilo claims descent from 'Navalius,' said to have founded Nvhi generations back.
claims.note: Navalius appears nowhere in the objective record - a family claim, invented backstory per the user, not drawn from any material source; Nuvilo himself admits he knows little else about Nvhi's actual history

claims.text: Nuvilo cites highway M9 (Nvhi -> Khan Ice); Nerkeli cites M7 (Puente Intercontinental -> Nvhi), which he flies regularly without having connected it to Nuvilo's family before this conversation.
claims.note: both routes are drawn directly from routes.highways

entries.summary: A traveler arriving at the fair meets Nuvilo, who orients them on what the Feria is celebrating, explains he has no official role there (just a visiting scholar), and describes what he writes about - historical inventors and travelers, and an unresolved puzzle about two chronicles of the same centuries that never agree.

claims.text: The Feria del Milenio celebrates 'a thousand years of Milkantis,' with exhibits honoring the world's cultures and building styles, its landscapes, its artifacts (codigos and redstone work among them), and its historical eras.
claims.note: the Feria itself is a session-level venue given directly by the user, not drawn from the objective record - see README §8 step 2

claims.text: Nuvilo holds no official role at the fair - unlike Nerkeli, running the airplane showcase, he's simply a visiting scholar 'following the path of knowledge.'
claims.note: matches Nuvilo's registered backstory

claims.text: Nuvilo writes about historical inventors and travelers, naming Daaxagoras and Pitaglorias (credited with the first atlas) and Darnis (who sailed south and found unmapped land).
Nuvilo describes an unsolved puzzle: two histories of the same centuries, written by different hands, that never reconcile.
claims.note: an informal, personal echo of CONFLICT-01 - Nuvilo doesn't cite it as such, he's speaking from his own scholarly frustration

location.as_named_in_dialog: the Feria del Milenio, by the airplane hangar

entries.summary: A traveler stops by Nerkeli's hangar at the fair. A genuine branch: they can ask about the plane and Nerkeli's flying (the M7 route, his freight work), or steer the talk toward the Feria itself, where Nerkeli turns out skeptical of the 'thousand years' framing - and, pressed on why, ends up explaining his duck/Daax theory.

claims.text: Nerkeli flies the M7 corridor (Puente Intercontinental -> Nvhi) as his regular assigned run, not for any business of his own - freight and the occasional passenger.
claims.note: matches routes.highways M7

claims.text: Despite flying that route for years, Nerkeli says he couldn't tell much about Nvhi itself - he turns around at the airstrip each time without properly seeing the place.
claims.note: consistent with Nerkeli's sampled knowledge not including the 'nvhi' location entry itself, only the M7 highway

claims.text: His freight is mixed: tools, building supplies, mail, and occasionally fragile merchant goods too delicate for boat or horse transport.
claims.note: invented character texture, not drawn from any material source - see README §8 step 2

claims.text: Nerkeli doubts the fair's 'thousand years of Milkantis' framing, saying he's heard the world's starting point told three incompatible ways across his travels, none of which line up.
claims.note: an informal, personal echo of CONFLICT-12 (three+ unreconciled 'start of the world' reference points) - Nerkeli doesn't cite it as such, he's speaking from travel-worn skepticism

claims.text: Nerkeli restates his running joke theory that ducks are the last living descendants of the Daax.
claims.note: same invented pet theory as in nuvilo_nerkeli_feria_del_milenio - offered explicitly as his own theory, not as history

location.as_named_in_dialog: la Plaza de las Culturas, Feria del Milenio

entries.summary: A visitor at the Plaza de las Culturas asks Döran what the pavilion is about. He orients them on the four castle replicas on display and the pavilion's AI-powered architectural holograms, then branches on the unfamiliar cities, the holograms' cost, or what "minor wonder" means.

claims.text: The Plaza de las Culturas is one of the Feria del Milenio's pavilions, honoring the diversity of architectural styles and urbanity across Milkantis, from small villages to great cities.
claims.note: the Plaza is a session-level venue given directly by the user, not drawn from the objective record - see README §8 step 2

claims.text: The Plaza displays castle replicas of Görff, Ciudad Dragón, and Salthos Cruzados, and the palace of Khan Icé - the fortresses of the largest cities.
claims.note: describes the pavilion's own exhibits, not itself a claim about the objective record

claims.text: The Plaza's pedestals sometimes display miniature AI-powered holograms of five other architectural marvels of Milkantis, built on a separate datapack - costly in energy, and if left running too long, the fabric of time itself grows tense and starts to crackle.
Döran calls Görff the oldest of the four represented castles, "curtida en más de una guerra" (weathered by more than one war).
claims.note: matches era_ensayo 'Las Guerras de Gorff' and the gorff location entry's castle/war history

claims.text: Döran says he knows Khan Icé's palace only through what train travelers tell him passing through, not firsthand.
claims.note: a personal admission, not independently verifiable

location.as_named_in_dialog: la Plaza de las Culturas, Feria del Milenio

entries.summary: Döran invites a visitor to ask about any of the four castles in the Plaza, branching per city: Salthos Cruzados (his own hometown, and its tie to the legendary prince Döran and the discovery of Plathinëa), Ciudad Dragón (its growth and his wariness over the destroyed map of Salthos Cruzados), Görff (its wars and its many travelers), and Khan Icé (where he speaks with more confidence than his firsthand knowledge supports).

claims.text: Prince Döran built the castle at Salthos Cruzados after the discovery of Plathinëa, and world cartography began there.
claims.note: matches the objective record closely (ensayo_i: castle built by prince Doran after Plathinea's discovery, ~72 d.V.; cartography begins here)

claims.text: This Döran shares his name with the legendary prince, and wonders whether that shaped his own path into maps and miniatures, or the other way around.
claims.note: a personal descent/namesake claim, given by the user as this character's backstory - see README §8 step 2; the objective record says nothing about the prince having descendants, so this is neither confirmed nor contradicted

claims.text: Plathinëa is described as 'the other half of the world' - the region discovered after Milkäan.
claims.note: matches the objective record's two-region split (Milkäan / Platinhüa) documented in unknown.md

claims.text: Ciudad Dragón grew from Península Dragón, absorbed a neighboring village, and became the largest city in all of Milkantis.
claims.note: matches the dragon_city location entry's merger narrative exactly

claims.text: Ciudad Dragón's mages are blamed for destroying the great map of Salthos Cruzados.
claims.note: matches the codigos concept entry: misuse of codigos by Dragon City's mages destroys the great map of Salthos Cruzados in 850 d.V.

claims.text: Görff's castle carries so many scars that an entire era was named for its wars, 'Las Guerras de Görff.'
claims.note: matches era_ensayo 'Las Guerras de Gorff' (era 2) and the gorff location entry's castle/war history

claims.text: Döran says more familiar faces pass through the fair from Görff than from anywhere else.
claims.note: a personal impression, not verifiable against the objective record

claims.text: Khan Icé is connected by rail to both Görff and Balhâm.
claims.note: matches the train_segment entries for Gorff-Khan Ice and Khan Ice-Balham

claims.text: Döran speculates, from the palace's defensive architecture, that Khan Icé served as a wartime refuge and possibly a capital 'when the world closed in on itself.'
claims.note: delivered as unconfirmed speculation - not sourced from Döran's own knowledge sample - but it happens to match the objective record: khan_ice's sources note 'refuge built end of era 1; world capital in Era del Confinamiento.' A confident bluff that landed on the truth, not a knowing lie; worth watching if a future retelling drops the hedge and states it as settled fact

location.as_named_in_dialog: la Plaza de las Culturas, Feria del Milenio

entries.summary: Döran muses that cultural differences are temporal as well as spatial, then branches on the oldest culture he knows well (Görff, leading into the Era del Daax), a rundown of the ages he can name, what era they're currently living in (the Era de la Magia), and a light tease about how poetic he sounds.

claims.text: Döran considers Görff, tied to 'Las Guerras de Görff,' the oldest culture among the four he can speak to with confidence - and admits a gap in what he knows between that era and the Era del Daax.

Döran describes the Era del Daax as the first age of the códigos and the era when architecture itself expanded most, noting the two chronicles disagree on when it began (360 d.V. vs. 294 d.V.) though both close it at 504 d.V.
claims.note: matches the objective record's own boundary mismatch exactly

claims.text: Döran names the Era de las Maravillas, starting around 804 d.V. with no end he knows of, among the ages he can speak to.

Döran says the present era is the Era de la Magia - when the tools that shape the world began transforming themselves, when people learned to 'mod the game' and bend the rules of the universe within this plane.
claims.note: the era's existence and dates are in the objective record; this specific framing is a session-given elaboration, plausible as written but not independently verifiable

location.as_named_in_dialog: la Plaza de las Culturas, frente a la réplica del Castillo de Görff, Feria del Milenio

entries.summary: Standing in front of the miniature replica of the Castillo de Görff, Khaoe and Farlis - both members of the Collective that now lives there - reflect on what the castle used to be versus what it is now.

claims.text: Before the Collective, and before the citadel was left abandoned, a tyrant ruled from the castle at Görff - his name no longer remembered.
claims.note: the objective gorff entry records the castle built in era 2 ('Las Guerras de Gorff') and an industrial restoration, but names no ruler and never uses the word 'tyrant' - compatible in timing, not confirmed in substance; first voiced here as the Collective's own telling of its origin, not drawn from either character's sampled knowledge

claims.text: Farlis calls it poetic justice that he and Khaoe now live in the same castle that once belonged to that tyrant.
claims.note: Farlis's own framing, given as his personal backstory reason for joining the Collective - not a lore claim to verify

claims.text: Khaoe pushes back on the 'poetic justice' framing - to her it's not symbolism, just that someone had to take up the stones.
claims.note: personal disposition, not a factual claim

location.as_named_in_dialog: la Plaza de las Culturas, frente a la réplica del Castillo de Görff, Feria del Milenio

entries.summary: Still by the castle replica, Farlis wonders what the Feria del Milenio's 'mil años' is actually counted from; Khaoe, just back from Lundria, says every temple there kept its own calendar; both conclude meaning shifts given enough time, or enough deliberate effort.

claims.text: Farlis says he was never told exactly what event the Feria's 'thousand years' framing counts from.
claims.note: echoes the same unreconciled origin-point problem documented as CONFLICT-12 (also independently echoed by Nerkeli in nerkeli_hangar_talk.json) - Farlis doesn't cite it as such, just voices the same gap

claims.text: Khaoe says every temple in Lundria kept its own calendar, as if the world began again at each door.
claims.note: the objective lundria entry records temple-building and the 'culto del cubo flotante de Lundria' (era 7) but says nothing about calendars specifically - plausible given the temple culture on record, not confirmed; Khaoe's own sampled knowledge of Lundria was bounded to the location's name/region/type, not this detail, so this is personal impression from her actual visit, not drawn from her sample

claims.text: Both agree a thing can end up meaning something else entirely, if enough time passes, or if someone puts in the work to change it.
claims.note: shared philosophical conclusion, not a factual claim

location.as_named_in_dialog: la Plaza de las Culturas, frente a la réplica del Castillo de Görff, Feria del Milenio

entries.summary: Still waiting by the castle replica, Khaoe and Farlis look out for their comrade Khaasan, who said he was coming straight to the fair but hasn't been sighted yet.

claims.text: Khaasan told Khaoe and Farlis he was coming straight to the Feria del Milenio.
claims.note: a social claim about a third party, nothing in the objective record to check it against

claims.text: Khaoe and Farlis expect Khaasan to arrive by griffon, and are watching the sky for it.
claims.note: the objective inhabitant record lists Khaasan's role as 'Teletraveller,' not a griffon rider - a genuine divergence, logged rather than silently reconciled per this file's own rule; could mean Khaoe and Farlis are simply wrong about how he travels, or that 'Teletraveller' and 'arrives by griffon' aren't actually mutually exclusive - left open, not resolved here

location.as_named_in_dialog: la Feria del Milenio, frente al Calendario Mecanográfico

entries.summary: A traveler asks Khaoe about the large new machine she's standing in front of. She explains what it is and what it's for, then, pressed to clarify her own aside about Lundria, admits she came back from her temple trip more confused about timekeeping than she left - and can't actually teach what she only half-remembers.

claims.text: The Calendario Mecanográfico is a new machine, inaugurated for the Feria del Milenio, that marks the current year on a moving timeline.
claims.note: a session-level venue fixture given directly by the user, not drawn from the objective record - see README §8 step 2

claims.text: Khaoe says every temple in Lundria disagreed on what year it was, each counting from something different, with nobody troubled by the mismatch.
claims.note: restates, in more detail, the same impression already on record from khaoe_farlis_lo_que_cambia_el_tiempo#2 - not drawn from a sampled hearsay item, just the same character carrying the same established impression into a later dialogue, so derived_from/oral_lore don't apply here

claims.text: Khaoe says she went to Lundria hoping to learn 'the' calendar there and came back without knowing which of the many was the real one.
claims.note: personal account of her own trip, not independently verifiable

claims.text: Khaoe vaguely recalls one temple that counted by moons and another that counted from the last time the whole town gathered.
claims.note: offered explicitly as a half-remembered, unreliable impression, not asserted as fact - she declines to 'teach' it and redirects to 'someone from Lundria' instead. None of these specific details appear in the objective lundria entry, which records only temple-building and the 'culto del cubo flotante de Lundria' (era 7) - plausible given that record, not confirmed or contradicted; Khaoe's own sampled knowledge of Lundria was bounded to the location's name/region/type, so this is personal impression from her visit, not drawn from her sample, consistent with the same caveat already logged for khaoe_farlis_lo_que_cambia_el_tiempo#2

location.as_named_in_dialog: la Feria del Milenio, un banco

entries.summary: Sitting on a bench watching people go by, Khaoe is approached by a traveler who's heard she's from the Collective. She confirms it, explains the horizontal organization when pressed, clarifies that Farlis isn't actually a prince, and names a few fellow Görff residents plus her closer comrades Farlis and Khaasan when asked who else is part of it.

claims.text: Khaoe confirms she's a member of the Collective, and jokes that either it shows or someone's been talking about her.
claims.note: matches her own registered backstory

claims.text: Khaoe says the Collective has spent years rebuilding Görff 'their own way,' and that people talk about it, for better or worse.
claims.note: a personal impression, not independently verifiable

claims.text: Khaoe clarifies that Farlis isn't literally a prince - his family has had money in Terfila for generations, but she's never been clear on the exact title, and he doesn't press the point either.
claims.note: matches Farlis's own registered backstory (aristocratic Terfila family, old money)

claims.text: Khaoe describes the Collective as horizontal in a specific sense: nobody leads just for arriving first, or for their surname.
claims.note: matches her own registered backstory's framing of the Collective

claims.text: Khaoe says she doesn't know an exact headcount for the Collective - more or less everyone living in Görff counts, given how the horizontal structure works.
claims.note: matches her own registered backstory, which frames the Collective as made up of 'the diversity of peoples that inhabit the Gorff farms and citadel'

claims.text: Khaoe names Bardaglis (a musician), Kristok Jakur (works the forge), and Dägna (runs the tavern) as fellow Görff residents, then Farlis and Khaasan as the comrades she sees most often.
claims.note: all five names match items in Khaoe's own sampled knowledge (inhabitant: Bardaglis (Gorff), inhabitant: Kristok Jakur (Gorff), inhabitant: Dägna (Gorff)) and their registered roles
